title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: The principal defined tier carrying every substantive restriction: any director (executive or otherwise); other key management personnel per the latest Annual Report; a C-suite executive, general manager, group manager or Company Secretary of the Westgold Group; key or senior contractors and consultants; and any other person designated in writing by the Board. Their spouse, children under 18, family or family-controlled trusts and family-controlled companies are deemed to be Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for authorisation: the Authorising Officer is the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee or the Managing Director.

tiers.name: Managing Director or any Executive Director
tiers.description: Authorising Officer is the Chair of the Board or, in their absence, the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Director (excluding the Chair)
tiers.description: Authorising Officer is the Managing Director or, in their absence, the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Key management personnel, 'C-suite' Executives, General Managers or Company Secretary
tiers.description: Key management personnel as set out in the latest Annual Report (excluding any Director), C-suite Executives, General Managers or the Company Secretary. Authorising Officer is the Managing Director or, in their absence, the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Westgold Group Managers or any other Designated Person
tiers.description: Residual row of the Authorising Officer table. Authorising Officer is the Company Secretary or, in their absence, the Managing Director.

tiers.name: any other employee or contractor of the Westgold Group
tiers.description: Westgold personnel who have not been notified that they are Designated Persons. Per the section 2.0 diagram they may deal in Company Securities provided they hold no Inside Information; the Blackout Periods, protection arrangement and security-granting restrictions in sections 5 and 6 are directed at Designated Persons, although the Board may impose ad-hoc restrictions on them under section 5.2.

tiers.name: Deemed Designated Persons (spouse, children under 18, family trusts and family-controlled companies)
tiers.description: A Designated Person's spouse or children (including stepchildren) under 18; a trust of which they, any family member or a family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary; and a company which they or their family control. These are deemed Designated Persons and carry the full set of restrictions.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the Designated Person's holding of Company Securities; operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (for example, hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf; or otherwise enable a Designated Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of Company Securities.

windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the ASX trading day immediately following the day on which Westgold's half-yearly results are released to the ASX and filed on SEDAR+

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose additional restrictions on Dealing without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion on any or all Designated Persons and on other Westgold personnel, including where the trade would otherwise be outside a Blackout Period. Such restrictions must be kept strictly confidential as the restriction itself may be Inside Information. The Board may also specify any other period as a Blackout Period under section 5.1.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include derivatives, equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether cash settled or not, and Dealing includes granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising or discharging an option or other right or obligation. A put and call package over vested unrestricted shares is a 'protection arrangement' which section 6.2 permits with consent under section 5.3, i.e. prior written authorisation on Form FM201 from the relevant Authorising Officer, valid five business days.
rules.evidence: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options and derivatives of any of the above (including, equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.

rules.detail: Protection arrangements over unvested Company Securities, including derivative positions in Westgold products, are prohibited at any time with no consent route.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities (or Westgold products in the derivatives markets): is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The same absolute prohibition applies to Company Securities that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and similar instruments are prohibited where they are short term or speculative; longer-dated non-speculative exchange traded positions are governed instead by the section 6.2 protection arrangement consent regime.
rules.evidence: This prohibition includes short term direct Dealing in Company Securities as well as transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements limiting the economic risk of a holding are a protection arrangement; over vested, unlocked securities they are permitted with prior written consent under section 5.3, exercised in the Authorising Officer's absolute discretion without reasons.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Company Securities ... otherwise, requires consent under section 5.3.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging unvested securities, expressly extending to Company Securities held beneficially for the Designated Person in trust or under an incentive plan.
rules.evidence: operate to limit the economic risk of any Designated Person's security holding (for example, hedging arrangements) including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf

rules.detail: Securities subject to a holding lock cannot be hedged at any time, even with consent.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Company Securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.tier: any other employee or contractor of the Westgold Group
rules.detail: Section 6.2 is addressed to Designated Persons only; non-designated employees and contractors are not covered, subject to the Board's power under section 5.2 to impose ad-hoc restrictions on them.

Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward, collar or exchangeable structure both limits economic risk and, if it involves security over the shares, engages section 6.3; each requires prior written consent under section 5.3 and neither is available over unvested or holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable a Designated Person to profit from a decrease in the market price of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is treated as a protection arrangement, but only to the extent it goes 'beyond the Designated Person's holding of Company Securities'; a covered position within the holding, as in a collar, is not short selling for this purpose. Where it is caught it is prohibited over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise requires section 5.3 consent.
rules.evidence: entering into protection arrangements includes entering into transactions which: amount to "short selling" of securities beyond the Designated Person's holding of Company Securities

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and the Dealing definition does not extend to it, although a stock loan would ordinarily transfer title and so involve a disposal within the Dealing definition.

Contracts for difference are named in the no speculative trading prohibition; the ban bites where the transaction is short term or speculative. A CFD would in any event be a protection arrangement if it limits economic risk.
rules.evidence: transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference and other similar instruments, which are short term or speculative

rules.detail: The second paragraph of section 6.3 permits a margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities with prior written consent under section 5.3. The first paragraph, however, states that Designated Persons may not 'at any time' grant security over unvested or holding-locked securities 'or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities' - a limb which on its face is not confined to unvested securities and sits awkwardly with the consent route in the second paragraph.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities, except with prior written consent under section 5.3.

rules.detail: Unvested and holding-locked securities can never be used in a margin lending arrangement or as security, at any time and with no consent route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security by charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise over vested unlocked Company Securities, to secure the Designated Person's own obligations or those of a third party, directly or indirectly, is permitted with prior written consent under section 5.3.
rules.evidence: grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party ... except with prior written consent under section 5.3.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on granting security over unvested Company Securities.
rules.evidence: may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Same absolute ban for securities subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Any secured financing over vested unlocked Company Securities, whatever its form, requires prior written consent under section 5.3; the prohibition is drafted around granting security to secure 'any obligation' of the Designated Person or a third party, so it captures a bank facility secured on the collared shares as well as a classic margin loan. Section 8.0 then expressly exempts a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement.
rules.evidence: except with prior written consent under section 5.3.

rules.detail: No secured financing of any kind may be taken over unvested or holding-locked Company Securities.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Blanket ban on short-term or speculative trading, with no defined holding period, months or basis; it extends to derivative market transactions that are short term or speculative.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.

exemption_authority: Section 5.4: the relevant Authorising Officer has discretion to approve Dealings during a Blackout Period 'or other Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by this Policy', on execution of Form FM201 with copy to the Company Secretary. Exceptional circumstances are assessed case by case in the Authorising Officer's absolute discretion and may include severe financial hardship or compliance with a court order or court enforceable undertaking. The decision may be made without reasons, is final and binding, may be withdrawn if circumstances change, and must be kept strictly confidential.
jurisdiction_overlays: Canadian securities laws and the Criminal Code (Canada), as a TSX-listed issuer
SEDAR+ filing of results, which conditions the end of each Blackout Period

SEDI insider reporting for 'reporting insiders': initial report within 10 days, and reports within 5 days of a change in beneficial ownership or in an interest, right or obligation associated with a related financial instrument, or on entering into, materially amending or terminating an arrangement altering economic exposure to the Company

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Company Securities, to secure any obligation of that Designated Person or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities, except with prior written consent under section 5.3.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, the loan leg of a funded collar is expressly contemplated and available over vested unlocked shares with prior written consent, rather than banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not, at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Company Securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock ... or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The margin lending limb of the first paragraph of section 6.3 is not on its face confined to unvested securities and appears to contradict the consent route in the second paragraph, so the facility should be documented as a secured term loan rather than a margin loan and the Company's written position on the inconsistency obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may, at any time: ... a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Lender enforcement is an express exemption available at any time, including during a Blackout Period, which removes the usual objection that a bank cannot realise its collateral without putting the executive in breach; the Designated Person must still advise the Authorising Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Securities means all securities issued by the Company and includes shares, share rights, performance rights, options and derivatives of any of the above (including, equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of an OTC collar are Company Securities in their own right, so entering, amending or unwinding them are Dealings requiring authorisation and are barred in Blackout Periods absent exceptional circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: including Company Securities held beneficially (for example, in trust or under an incentive plan) on that Designated Person's behalf
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares held through an employee share trust cannot be collared while unvested or locked, so the collateral pool must be limited to fully vested, released holdings.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from close of trading on the ASX on 31 March and 30 September, until commencement of trading on the ASX trading day immediately following the announcement of Westgold's quarterly reports
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Quarterly as well as half and full year blackouts leave narrow open windows, so entry, roll and unwind of the collar must be tightly scheduled or brought within the section 5.4 exceptional circumstances discretion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may impose, without notice and in its sole and absolute discretion, additional restrictions on Dealing ... Any restriction communicated by the Board ... must be kept strictly confidential as the restriction itself may be considered Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive may be unable to tell the bank why a scheduled roll or unwind cannot proceed, so the trade documentation must tolerate unexplained delay.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written authorisation under this Policy may be withdrawn by the Authorising Officer in writing at any time during the clearance period ... having regard to the broader reputational, governance and other implications of the proposed Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Authorisation for the collar is revocable on reputational grounds at any point in the five business day window, so pricing should not be locked before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting insiders must also file an insider trading report within five (5) days if the reporting insider enters into, materially amends, or terminates an agreement, arrangement or understanding that (i) has the effect of altering, directly or indirectly, the reporting insider's economic exposure to the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and any material amendment or termination must be publicly disclosed on SEDI within five days, so the structure cannot be kept confidential and the parties should agree disclosure wording in advance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Under no circumstances should Designated Persons engage in short-term or speculative trading in Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and absolute, so a short-dated or highly geared collar risks being characterised as speculative even where consent for the protection arrangement is available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any authorisation to trade by the Authorising Officer under this section 5.4 is not an endorsement to trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Consent to the collar carries no representation by Westgold that the structure complies with the Policy or the law, so the bank should not treat the Form FM201 as a compliance opinion.

summary: Westgold is one of the few ASX policies under which a funded collar is affirmatively available, but only over fully vested Company Securities that are not subject to a holding lock, and only with prior written consent. Section 6.2 treats the put and call legs as a 'protection arrangement', prohibited absolutely over unvested or holding-locked securities and otherwise permitted with consent under section 5.3; section 6.3 does the same for the loan leg, prohibiting any charge, mortgage or pledge over Company Securities to secure any obligation except with prior written consent, so the bank's security is contemplated rather than banned. Consent is given by the relevant Authorising Officer on Form FM201, is valid five business days, may be withdrawn on reputational grounds and may be refused in absolute discretion without reasons; Dealings are otherwise barred in four Blackout Periods a year and during confidential Board-imposed ad-hoc restrictions, subject to the section 5.4 exceptional circumstances discretion which can approve 'other Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited'. Critically, section 8.0 expressly exempts a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement, so enforcement of the bank's collateral does not itself breach the Policy. Two cautions: the first paragraph of section 6.3 contains an unqualified margin lending prohibition that sits awkwardly with the consent route, so the facility should be documented as a secured term loan and the Company's position confirmed in writing; and as a TSX-listed issuer, entering into, materially amending or terminating the collar triggers SEDI insider reports within five days for reporting insiders.
